This addresses the dispute by reminding people that God has authority to designate the direction of worship. The controversy tests whether people trust revelation when worship practice is redirected.

phrases.translation: He guides whoever He wills to the Straight Path.”
phrases.explanation: God guides people to the right way, including the direction and practice He commands. The verse connects obedience in worship with divine guidance. It calls listeners to follow God’s instruction rather than argue over directions as though one were beyond His authority. A sacred direction has meaning because God appoints it, not because of geography alone.

phrases.translation: And so We have made you ˹believers˺ an upright community
phrases.explanation: The believers are made an upright community, balanced and committed to justice. This standing carries responsibility, not a claim to moral perfection. The phrase introduces a role connected to witness and faithful practice in the world. Uprightness here carries duties of fairness, faithfulness, and representing the message responsibly.

phrases.translation: so that you may be witnesses over humanity and that the Messenger may be a witness over you.
phrases.explanation: The community is assigned a role of witness to humanity, while the Messenger bears witness over them. This responsibility involves conveying and embodying the message. The verse links communal honor with accountability to follow the Prophet’s guidance. Their witness is meaningful only when their lives reflect the guidance they convey.

phrases.translation: We assigned your former direction of prayer only to distinguish those who would remain faithful to the Messenger from those who would lose faith.
phrases.explanation: The previous prayer direction served as a test of fidelity to the Messenger. The change distinguished those who trusted his guidance from those who turned away. The verse explains the purpose of the test without treating the former direction as meaningless or the new one as arbitrary.

phrases.translation: It was certainly a difficult test except for those ˹rightly˺ guided by Allah.
phrases.explanation: Changing a familiar practice could be difficult, but guidance helped believers respond faithfully. The verse recognizes the challenge rather than dismissing it. It shows that obedience may require trust when a command changes, and that God’s guidance supports those who seek it. The episode therefore tests trust in the Messenger rather than attachment to custom.

phrases.translation: And Allah would never discount your ˹previous acts of˺ faith.
phrases.explanation: God will not let earlier acts of faith go unrewarded, including prayers performed before the direction changed. The verse reassures believers that obedience at an earlier time remains valid. God knows their sincerity and does not waste their faithful actions. Sincere obedience is not expected to be effortless, but guidance makes it possible.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to humanity
phrases.explanation: The conclusion names God’s kindness and mercy toward people. It explains the reassurance about past prayer and the guidance through changing circumstances. The verse presents divine instruction as accompanied by care, not as a trap intended to invalidate sincere worship. Their prayers remain honored even though the direction was later changed by command.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We see you ˹O Prophet˺ turning your face towards heaven.
phrases.explanation: God acknowledges that the Prophet has been looking toward heaven, awaiting instruction about the prayer direction. The phrase presents his concern as known to God. It introduces the change that will answer the Prophet’s hope. His attention expresses hope for guidance, not dissatisfaction with God’s earlier command.

phrases.translation: Now We will make you turn towards a direction ˹of prayer˺ that will please you.
phrases.explanation: God promises a prayer direction that will please the Prophet. The change is presented as divine instruction and a response to his hope, not a choice made independently. The phrase prepares the community for a new direction in worship. The change confirms that the Prophet’s concern is answered through revelation.

phrases.translation: So turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque ˹in Mecca˺—wherever you are, turn your faces towards it.
phrases.explanation: The command establishes the Sacred Mosque in Mecca as the direction of prayer. Believers are to face it wherever they are. This shared orientation unites the community in worship and marks a specific instruction from God. This instruction establishes the qibla for prayer wherever the worshippers may be.

phrases.translation: Those who were given the Scripture certainly know this to be the truth from their Lord.
phrases.explanation: The verse says that people given earlier scripture can recognize the truth of the command. It situates the qibla change within the revelation known to them, while the surrounding debate includes those who dispute it. The statement concerns recognition of the message in this historical context.

phrases.translation: And Allah is never unaware of what they do
phrases.explanation: God knows the responses of those who accept or resist the instruction. Nothing in the debate is hidden from Him. The closing phrase assures believers that their obedience is seen and warns opponents that their actions remain accountable. Divine awareness includes responses to this command and every other deed.

phrases.translation: Even if you were to bring every proof to the People of the Book,
phrases.explanation: The verse says that abundant evidence would not persuade the disputants described. It emphasizes the role of unwillingness, not a lack of available argument. The phrase concerns a particular historical dispute and should not be generalized to all Jews or Christians. The warning prepares the Prophet to stay firm even when debate continues.

phrases.translation: they would not accept your direction ˹of prayer˺, nor would you accept theirs; nor would any of them accept the direction ˹of prayer˺ of another.
phrases.explanation: The passage acknowledges that the communities have different prayer directions and are unlikely to adopt one another’s practice. It discourages trying to satisfy every group by abandoning revelation. The point is fidelity to God’s instruction, not contempt for other people’s worship. Each community is responsible for following the guidance it has received.

phrases.translation: And if you were to follow their desires after ˹all˺ the knowledge that has come to you,
phrases.explanation: The warning concerns abandoning revealed knowledge to follow others’ preferences. The verse addresses the Prophet rhetorically to underscore the seriousness of trading guidance for approval. It cautions believers against letting social pressure replace their understanding of God’s command. Approval from opponents must not become a higher priority than revelation.

phrases.translation: then you would certainly be one of the wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: Following desires against known guidance would be wrongdoing. The phrase concludes the warning with a clear statement of responsibility. It emphasizes that knowledge brings accountability and that faithfulness requires holding to the instruction received. The strong wording marks the seriousness of knowingly abandoning revealed truth.

phrases.translation: Those We have given the Scripture recognize this ˹Prophet˺ as they recognize their own children.
phrases.explanation: The verse describes some people given scripture as recognizing the Prophet clearly. The comparison conveys strong familiarity, but the claim is limited to those who recognize him and should not be generalized to every member of a community. It explains the gravity of concealing what they know.

phrases.translation: Yet a group of them hides the truth knowingly
phrases.explanation: Some deliberately conceal what they recognize. The verse criticizes intentional concealment, not honest disagreement or uncertainty. The phrase calls for truthful speech about revelation and stresses that knowledge brings responsibility. Awareness makes the choice to conceal truth especially serious in this account. The text contrasts their deliberate silence with the responsibility to bear witness truthfully.

phrases.translation: ˹This is˺ the truth from your Lord, so do not ever be one of those who doubt
phrases.explanation: The message is affirmed as truth from God, and the Prophet is urged to remain certain. The statement provides reassurance amid disputes about revelation and prayer direction. It calls believers to trust the source of the guidance rather than be unsettled by opposition. The reassurance addresses pressure created by arguments over the new direction.

phrases.translation: Everyone turns to their own direction ˹of prayer˺.
phrases.explanation: Different communities have their appointed directions of prayer. The verse acknowledges this diversity while directing attention toward obedience to God. It does not present competing directions as grounds for hostility, but as part of how communities practice worship. The acknowledged difference is not permission to neglect God’s instruction.

phrases.translation: So compete with one another in doing good.
phrases.explanation: Rather than quarrel over differences, people are urged to excel in good deeds. The phrase shifts the focus from ritual dispute to moral action. The measure of faith includes what people do, and good works can be pursued across communities. Good conduct offers a constructive response to disagreement and rivalry.

phrases.translation: Wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together ˹for judgment˺.
phrases.explanation: People will ultimately be gathered by God for judgment wherever they are now. The promise makes geography and community divisions temporary. It reminds everyone that final accountability is shared before God. The promise applies to all people, not only one nation or place. No earthly distance can prevent the gathering when God has decreed it.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything
phrases.explanation: God has full power to gather people and judge them. This attribute supports the promise and closes the verse with certainty. No distance or human boundary can prevent His judgment. The attribute assures believers that the promised gathering is entirely possible. Human disagreement cannot weaken God’s power to fulfill His promise.

phrases.translation: Wherever you are ˹O Prophet˺, turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque.
phrases.explanation: The command again directs the Prophet to face the Sacred Mosque in prayer. Repetition emphasizes the importance of the new qibla and makes the instruction clear. The place is a central point of worship for the community. The repeated wording removes uncertainty about the place toward which prayer is directed.

phrases.translation: This is certainly the truth from your Lord.
phrases.explanation: The direction is affirmed as a true command from God. The statement answers doubt and grounds the practice in revelation rather than preference. Believers are asked to trust the source of the instruction. Revelation, rather than communal preference, is the basis for this practice. The statement confirms the direction as an act of worship required by God.

phrases.translation: And Allah is never unaware of what you ˹all˺ do
phrases.explanation: God knows whether people obey or resist the command. The phrase offers assurance that faithful practice is seen and that rejection remains accountable. It concludes by emphasizing divine awareness of the community’s conduct. The reminder includes both the Prophet and the wider community. It also reassures the faithful that obedience is never overlooked.

phrases.translation: Wherever you are ˹O Prophet˺, turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque.
phrases.explanation: The instruction is repeated to reinforce the qibla for the Prophet. Repetition underscores that the change is a settled command, not a temporary preference. It marks the Sacred Mosque as the shared direction for worship. Reaffirming the instruction supports consistency in communal worship. The command is repeated for clarity and firm observance across the community.

phrases.translation: And wherever you ˹believers˺ are, face towards it,
phrases.explanation: The believers are included wherever they may be. The shared direction creates unity in prayer across distance and location. The command applies to the whole community rather than only those physically near the Sacred Mosque. Distance from Mecca does not exempt believers from the shared practice.

phrases.translation: so that people will have no argument against you, except the wrongdoers among them.
phrases.explanation: The clear instruction removes a legitimate objection, though some may continue to argue unjustly. The verse distinguishes honest questions from opposition that persists despite clarity. It explains the public purpose of the qibla and warns that not all criticism is sincere. Persistent rejection after clear instruction is distinguished from sincere inquiry.

phrases.translation: Do not fear them; fear Me,
phrases.explanation: Believers are told not to let human pressure outweigh reverence for God. Fear of God here means obedience and accountability, not panic. The command encourages steadiness when people criticize the change in prayer direction. The call redirects anxiety from public opinion toward accountability to God.

phrases.translation: so that I may ˹continue to˺ perfect My favour upon you and so you may be ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation: God’s favor includes completing guidance and directing the community toward the right path. The qibla instruction is presented as part of that favor. The verse links obedience with divine guidance and encourages believers to remain grateful and steadfast. The final purpose is guidance, not merely a change in outward ritual.

phrases.translation: Since We have sent you a messenger from among yourselves—
phrases.explanation: God reminds the audience that He has sent a messenger from their own people. His familiar language and setting make the message accessible, while his mission comes from God. The verse introduces several connected duties of this messenger and presents his presence as a divine favor.

phrases.translation: reciting to you Our revelations,
phrases.explanation: The messenger recites God’s revelations so the community can hear and learn them. Recitation makes the message public and preserves its words for reflection. This is not merely performance, but a means of communicating divine guidance to people in a form they can understand and remember.

phrases.translation: purifying you,
phrases.explanation: The messenger’s mission includes helping people become morally and spiritually purified. This involves moving away from wrongdoing and cultivating sincere faith and good conduct. Purification complements learning: revelation is meant to shape the heart and behavior, not remain information without practical effect.  Its goal is transformation of character, not outward conformity alone.

phrases.translation: teaching you the Book and wisdom,
phrases.explanation: He teaches the revealed Book and wisdom, helping the community understand guidance and apply it well. The phrase joins scripture with sound judgment in practice. Instruction enables people to benefit from revelation, distinguish right from wrong, and live according to God’s direction.  Wisdom helps ensure that knowledge guides decisions and behavior.

phrases.translation: and teaching you what you never knew—
phrases.explanation: The messenger also brings knowledge the audience did not previously possess. Revelation expands human understanding and corrects ignorance. The verse portrays his teaching as a comprehensive gift: recitation, purification, instruction, and new knowledge all contribute to the community’s guidance.  This learning equips believers to respond to life with informed faith.

phrases.translation: remember Me; I will remember you.
phrases.explanation: Believers are commanded to remember God through devotion, gratitude, and obedience. God’s remembrance of them signifies His care and favor, not a need to be reminded. The reciprocal wording encourages a close relationship: those who keep God in their thoughts and actions can trust in His gracious attention.

phrases.translation: And thank Me,
phrases.explanation: Gratitude is directed to God, the giver of blessings and guidance. Thankfulness includes recognizing gifts, praising their source, and using them responsibly. Coming after the reminder of the messenger, the command invites believers to appreciate revelation rather than take it for granted.  Such gratitude turns awareness of blessings into a pattern of worship.

phrases.translation: and never be ungrateful
phrases.explanation: The verse warns against denying God’s blessings or responding to them with disobedience. Gratitude and ingratitude are expressed in conduct as well as words. Believers should not let hardship or familiarity erase awareness of divine generosity and the guidance they have received.  The warning calls for gratitude in action throughout daily life.

phrases.translation: O believers! Seek comfort in patience and prayer.
phrases.explanation: Believers are instructed to seek support through patient perseverance and prayer. Patience means holding firm to what is right during hardship, while prayer renews dependence on God. Together they provide spiritual strength rather than promising an effortless life. The direct address encourages the community to use these practices actively.

phrases.translation: Allah is truly with those who are patient
phrases.explanation: God’s nearness to the patient is a promise of support, care, and reward. Patience is not passive surrender to injustice, but steadfastness in obedience and hardship. The verse gives reassurance that those who endure faithfully are not abandoned, even when relief is not immediate.  The promise encourages perseverance through challenges of every kind.

phrases.translation: Never say that those martyred in the cause of Allah are dead—in fact, they are alive!
phrases.explanation: Those killed in God’s cause are not to be regarded as having simply vanished or lost their ultimate life. The verse affirms a special life with God beyond ordinary perception. It offers comfort to the bereaved and honors sacrifice, while leaving the nature of that life to divine knowledge.

phrases.translation: But you do not perceive it
phrases.explanation: The living state of the martyrs is beyond ordinary human perception. People cannot observe or measure every reality by what is visible in this world. The phrase asks believers to trust revelation about the unseen and not equate physical death with ultimate nonexistence.  Trust in the unseen sustains hope after a painful loss.

phrases.translation: We will certainly test you with a touch of fear and famine and loss of property, life, and crops.
phrases.explanation: The verse warns that believers will face trials including fear, hunger, and losses affecting wealth, people, and harvests. These hardships are described as tests, not proof that God has abandoned them. Naming varied forms of loss prepares the community for difficulty and frames endurance as part of faith.

phrases.translation: Give good news to those who patiently endure—
phrases.explanation: The command to give good news assures those who remain steadfast that their response matters. Endurance is not denial of grief, but maintaining faith and right conduct through it. The phrase leads into the words they say when disaster strikes, showing patience as both an inner conviction and a spoken remembrance.

phrases.translation: who, when faced with a disaster, say,
phrases.explanation: The patient are identified by their response when calamity arrives. Their words reflect a conviction about belonging to God and returning to Him. This statement does not deny pain or loss, it gives hardship a wider spiritual frame and helps believers respond with trust rather than despair.

phrases.translation: “Surely to Allah we belong and to Him we will ˹all˺ return.”
phrases.explanation: This declaration recognizes that people and their lives belong to God and that all will return to Him. It can be spoken in grief as an expression of trust, not as a claim that loss is painless. The words affirm divine ownership, final accountability, and hope beyond worldly hardship.

phrases.translation: They are the ones who will receive Allah’s blessings and mercy.
phrases.explanation: Those who respond to hardship with patience and remembrance receive God’s blessings and mercy. The verse promises divine care without suggesting that believers will never suffer. Their steadfast response is met with grace, and their loss is understood within a relationship with the Most Merciful.

phrases.translation: And it is they who are ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation: The patient are described as guided because they understand their dependence on God and remain oriented toward Him in hardship. Guidance here is visible in their response to trials. The verse closes the sequence by connecting patience, remembrance, mercy, and spiritual direction.  Their choices show how guidance can be lived during adversity.

phrases.translation: Indeed, ˹the hills of˺ Ṣafa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.
phrases.explanation: Ṣafa and Marwah are affirmed as sacred symbols connected with worship. The verse addresses concern about the ritual walk between them, making clear that their use does not compromise devotion to God. Their significance is established by divine designation and the rites associated with pilgrimage.

phrases.translation: So whoever performs the pilgrimage or minor pilgrimage, let them walk between ˹the two hills˺.
phrases.explanation: Pilgrims performing the major or minor pilgrimage are instructed to make the ritual walk between Ṣafa and Marwah. This practice is part of the pilgrimage rites, not worship of the hills themselves. The verse preserves the rite and clarifies its place within worship directed to God alone.

phrases.translation: And whoever does good willingly, Allah is truly Appreciative, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: God appreciates voluntary good and fully knows the intentions behind it. The phrase encourages sincere acts beyond bare obligation while affirming that no good deed is overlooked. Divine appreciation is not limited by human recognition, God knows both what people do and why they do it.

phrases.translation: Those who hide the clear proofs and guidance that We have revealed—
phrases.explanation: The verse condemns concealing clear evidence and guidance revealed by God. The wrongdoing lies in withholding what should be communicated, especially when people depend on truthful teaching. This warning addresses deliberate concealment and does not equate sincere uncertainty or disagreement with knowingly hiding revelation.  Concealment can mislead others and obstruct their access to guidance.

phrases.translation: after We made it clear for humanity in the Book—
phrases.explanation: The guidance had been clarified in scripture for people, making concealment especially serious. Revelation is given as a means of guidance, not private knowledge to be suppressed for advantage. The phrase stresses public responsibility to communicate what God has made clear.  Its purpose is to guide people, so it must not be withheld.

phrases.translation: will be condemned by Allah and ˹all˺ those who condemn
phrases.explanation: Those who conceal guidance incur condemnation from God and from those who rightly condemn such wrongdoing. The severe warning reflects the harm done when people are deprived of truth. It underscores accountability for misusing knowledge and prepares for the following verse’s offer of repentance.  Those who suppress it answer for the resulting harm.

phrases.translation: As for those who repent, mend their ways, and let the truth be known,
phrases.explanation: The warning is not closed to anyone who turns back sincerely. Repentance must be accompanied by correcting one’s conduct and making the truth public again. This full response repairs both the person’s relationship with God and the harm caused by earlier concealment.  Reform should address the consequences of earlier wrongdoing.

phrases.translation: they are the ones to whom I will turn ˹in forgiveness˺,
phrases.explanation: God promises to turn in mercy toward those who repent, reform, and disclose the truth. Forgiveness is linked with genuine change rather than words alone. The phrase offers hope to people who have committed serious wrong, while showing that restoration requires honest correction.  Divine forgiveness restores hope while still calling for accountability.

phrases.translation: for I am the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: God describes Himself as accepting repentance and showing mercy. These names ground the promise in divine generosity and assure people that sincere return is welcomed. The verse balances the previous warning: deliberate concealment is grave, but repentance and restoration remain possible.  The verse ends with hope in God’s mercy for those who turn back.

phrases.translation: Surely those who disbelieve and die as disbelievers are condemned by Allah, the angels, and all of humanity
phrases.explanation: The verse speaks of those who persist in disbelief until death and describes their severe condemnation. Its focus is a final rejection, not a temporary doubt or a person who later repents. The mention of God, angels, and humanity underscores the gravity of knowingly turning away from truth.

phrases.translation: They will be in Hell forever.
phrases.explanation: The verse describes the lasting consequence for those who die in persistent disbelief. The warning is serious and emphasizes the finality of that choice. It is a statement about the fate of the condemned described in the preceding verse, not a judgment believers should casually assign to individuals.

phrases.translation: Their punishment will not be lightened,
phrases.explanation: The punishment is described as not being reduced. This emphasizes the seriousness of the outcome and warns against treating rejection as inconsequential. The verse belongs to a passage that contrasts the severe end of persistent disbelief with the possibility of repentance shown earlier.  The statement stresses that justice is not suspended after death.

phrases.translation: nor will they be delayed ˹from it˺
phrases.explanation: They will not be granted postponement from the punishment once its time comes. The phrase underscores the certainty and accountability of the final judgment. It encourages people to respond to guidance in life, when repentance and reform remain possible.  The warning makes present choices consequential and calls people to reconsider.

phrases.translation: Your God is ˹only˺ One God.
phrases.explanation: The verse declares that God is one, rejecting the idea that divinity is divided among rivals. This affirmation of oneness is central to the chapter’s call to worship and gratitude. It directs every person toward the same Lord rather than competing objects of devotion.  This teaching is the foundation for the worship and moral guidance that follow.

phrases.translation: There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—
phrases.explanation: No being deserves worship besides God. The phrase clarifies that divine unity has practical consequences: worship, reliance, and ultimate devotion belong to Him alone. It excludes partners without denying that created beings may have honor or influence within creation.  The declaration rules out directing acts of worship toward any created being.

phrases.translation: the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: God’s oneness is joined with the attributes of compassion and mercy. This portrays the Creator not only as sovereign but as deeply merciful toward creation. The names encourage hope and trust, grounding worship in recognition of both God’s greatness and His care.  Mercy is emphasized as a defining attribute through which people know their Lord.

phrases.translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth;
phrases.explanation: The immense creation of the heavens and earth is presented as a sign for reflective people. Their existence and order point beyond themselves to the Creator’s power and wisdom. The verse invites observation of the world as a source of reflection, not as an object of worship.

phrases.translation: the alternation of the day and the night;
phrases.explanation: The regular succession of day and night offers signs in the rhythms of life. Their change brings opportunities for work, rest, and worship. Observing this dependable pattern can lead people to recognize order and purpose rather than taking the conditions of life for granted.  The predictable cycle sustains human life while reminding people of their dependence.

phrases.translation: the ships that sail the sea for the benefit of humanity;
phrases.explanation: Ships crossing the sea serve human needs through travel and trade. Their movement depends on skill, materials, and conditions God has made possible. The verse points to the ways people benefit from creation and should respond with reflection and gratitude.  Human travel and commerce rely on natural conditions people did not create.

phrases.translation: the rain sent down by Allah from the skies, reviving the earth after its death;
phrases.explanation: Rain revives land that appeared lifeless, making growth and nourishment possible. The image of renewed earth also evokes God’s power to bring life after death. The verse asks people to notice how essential provision comes through processes beyond their control.  Renewal after barrenness makes divine power visible in ordinary experience.

phrases.translation: the scattering of all kinds of creatures throughout;
phrases.explanation: The many creatures spread across the earth display variety and order in living creation. Their existence points to the breadth of God’s power and provision. People are invited to reflect on life beyond their own needs and recognize their place within a larger created world.

phrases.translation: the shifting of the winds;
phrases.explanation: Changing winds influence weather and the movement of clouds, bringing both benefit and challenge. Their shifts are part of the dynamic processes sustaining life. The phrase invites attention to natural patterns that may seem ordinary but reveal dependence on forces people do not command.  Their movement reminds observers that nature is ordered beyond human control.

phrases.translation: and the clouds drifting between the heavens and the earth—˹in all of this˺ are surely signs for people of understanding
phrases.explanation: Clouds move through the space between heaven and earth, carrying rain and displaying the workings of creation. These signs are especially recognized by people who reflect thoughtfully. The verse gathers natural phenomena into a call to reason, gratitude, and recognition of God rather than treating them as disconnected accidents.

phrases.translation: Still there are some who take others as Allah’s equal—
phrases.explanation: Some people give others a status that belongs uniquely to God. This can involve devotion or obedience that rivals worship of the Creator. The verse warns against misplaced allegiance while leaving the specific cases to God’s judgment.  The warning addresses the serious error of sharing divine devotion with others.

phrases.translation: they love them as they should love Allah—
phrases.explanation: Their attachment to these supposed equals takes on the intensity and devotion owed to God. The issue is not ordinary affection for people, but elevating created beings into objects of ultimate devotion. The phrase examines the heart’s priorities and the way misplaced love can shape worship.

phrases.translation: but the ˹true˺ believers love Allah even more.
phrases.explanation: Believers’ love for God surpasses every competing attachment. This love grounds their loyalty and trust in the Creator. The contrast challenges people to consider whether their devotion is centered on God or subordinated to created powers and desires.  Their love is expressed through allegiance and obedience to God.

phrases.translation: If only the wrongdoers could see the ˹horrible˺ punishment ˹awaiting them˺,
phrases.explanation: The verse says that wrongdoers would understand the seriousness of their choices if they could witness the coming punishment. Their present confidence may obscure the consequences. The warning invites reflection before judgment, while there is still time to change course.  The warning is meant to awaken reflection before that future arrives.

phrases.translation: they would certainly realize that all power belongs to Allah
phrases.explanation: At judgment, people will recognize that ultimate power belongs to God alone. No alleged partner or worldly authority can protect anyone against His decision. This realization exposes the error of directing ultimate devotion toward anything besides the Creator.  This truth will become unmistakable when worldly powers can no longer intervene.

phrases.translation: and that Allah is indeed severe in punishment
phrases.explanation: God’s punishment is severe for wrongdoing, a reality the verse insists should not be ignored. The statement balances the previous emphasis on divine power and warns that mercy must not be used as an excuse for injustice. It calls for reverence and accountability.  The warning is a call to turn away from wrongdoing while there is time.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider the Day˺ when those who misled others will disown their followers—
phrases.explanation: On the Day of Judgment, leaders who led people astray will reject their followers. The verse warns against blindly trusting influential figures who encourage wrongdoing. Authority and popularity cannot shield anyone from responsibility for their own choices.  Their influence cannot remove the followers’ own responsibility before God.

phrases.translation: when they face the torment—
phrases.explanation: The disowning occurs when both leaders and followers confront punishment. In that moment, worldly confidence gives way to the reality of accountability. The phrase emphasizes that consequences become undeniable at judgment, though the warning is given now so people may act differently.  The moment reveals the consequences that worldly status had concealed.

phrases.translation: and the bonds that united them will be cut off
phrases.explanation: The ties that joined misleaders and followers will collapse. Alliances built around wrongdoing cannot endure before God’s judgment. The verse warns that social loyalty offers no lasting refuge when it is grounded in rejection of truth.  This judgment severs loyalties that once seemed strong and dependable.

phrases.translation: The ˹misled˺ followers will cry,
phrases.explanation: The followers express anguish after realizing that those they trusted have abandoned them. Their reaction shows the cost of surrendering moral judgment to others. The verse presents this regret as a warning to choose one’s influences carefully in life.  Their distress reflects a choice to follow without examining the message.

phrases.translation: “If only we could have a second chance, we would disown them as they disowned us.”
phrases.explanation: The followers wish for another chance so they could reject the leaders who misled them. The statement reveals regret, but it comes too late to undo their choices. The verse calls people to discern truth now rather than assuming they can reverse their decisions after judgment.

phrases.translation: And so Allah will make them remorseful of their misdeeds.
phrases.explanation: God will make them see and regret the consequences of their actions. Their remorse reflects the realization that their choices and loyalties led them astray. The verse links regret with wrongdoing, reminding readers that choices matter before their consequences become irreversible.  Recognition after judgment cannot undo the actions that caused regret.

phrases.translation: And they will never ˹be able to˺ leave the Fire
phrases.explanation: The verse describes the condemned as unable to escape the Fire. This completes the warning about misplaced allegiance and belated regret. It emphasizes the urgency of guidance and repentance in worldly life, while the chance to act remains open.  This finality contrasts with the present opportunity to repent and change.

phrases.translation: O humanity!
phrases.explanation: The address is universal, extending beyond one community or group. The instruction that follows concerns basic choices shared by all people. Its broad opening underlines that moral guidance and care for what one consumes are relevant to humanity as a whole.  The message therefore includes practical matters alongside spiritual belief.

phrases.translation: Eat from what is lawful and good on the earth
phrases.explanation: People are told to consume what is both lawful and wholesome. The guidance joins moral permissibility with goodness, encouraging choices that nourish rather than harm. The phrase recognizes the earth’s provisions as gifts while placing ethical limits on how people use them.  Lawful and wholesome choices respect both divine limits and human wellbeing.

phrases.translation: and do not follow Satan’s footsteps.
phrases.explanation: The warning against Satan’s footsteps describes gradual movement toward wrongdoing. People should not follow impulses and practices that lead away from God’s guidance. The wording encourages caution at the beginning of a harmful path, before small choices accumulate into serious disobedience.  The image cautions against gradual compromise, not only obvious rebellion.

phrases.translation: He is truly your sworn enemy
phrases.explanation: Satan is identified as a clear enemy of humanity, so his influence should not be trusted. The warning explains why people must be discerning about what they follow. Recognizing the danger helps believers resist deception and seek guidance from God instead.  Believers are urged to remain alert to false promises and harmful suggestions.

phrases.translation: He only incites you to commit evil and indecency,
phrases.explanation: Satan’s influence urges people toward evil and shameful conduct. The verse makes clear that such impulses should not be mistaken for guidance. Recognizing their source can help people resist them and choose actions consistent with God’s commands.  Such conduct harms people and draws them further from the path of righteousness.

phrases.translation: and to claim against Allah what you do not know
phrases.explanation: Satan also encourages people to speak about God without knowledge, inventing claims or rules and attributing them to Him. This is a serious misuse of speech and religious authority. The phrase calls for humility and evidence when discussing divine guidance.  Religious claims require care, since falsely speaking for God can mislead others.

phrases.translation: When it is said to them, “Follow what Allah has revealed,”
phrases.explanation: People are invited to follow God’s revealed guidance rather than inherited customs alone. Revelation provides a standard by which traditions can be assessed. The verse frames the ensuing response as a choice between guidance and unexamined imitation.  The appeal is to revelation as a guide for evaluating human custom.

phrases.translation: they reply, “No! We ˹only˺ follow what we found our forefathers practicing.”
phrases.explanation: The people defend their practices by appealing solely to what their ancestors did. Respect for family history does not make every inherited custom true. The verse warns against treating tradition as a substitute for evidence and thoughtful obedience to God.  The reply avoids considering whether the inherited practice is actually true.

phrases.translation: ˹Would they still do so,˺ even if their forefathers had ˹absolutely˺ no understanding or guidance
phrases.explanation: The rhetorical question exposes the danger of imitation without knowledge. If ancestors lacked understanding or guidance, copying them cannot lead to truth. The verse calls each generation to examine inherited beliefs and follow what is sound, rather than assuming age or custom guarantees correctness.  Guidance requires reasoned reflection, not merely repeating familiar habits.

phrases.translation: The example of the disbelievers ˹not responding to the Messenger’s warning˺ is like a flock not comprehending the calls and cries of the shepherd.
phrases.explanation: The verse compares people who refuse the Messenger’s warning to animals that hear a shepherd’s calls but do not grasp their meaning. The image concerns failure to respond to guidance, not lack of intelligence in general. It warns against hearing the message while refusing to reflect on it.

phrases.translation: ˹They are wilfully˺ deaf, dumb and blind so they have no understanding
phrases.explanation: The description of deafness, muteness, and blindness is figurative: they do not use their faculties to recognize truth. Their lack of understanding follows from deliberate refusal, not a physical disability. The verse urges listeners to be receptive to warning and to engage thoughtfully with revelation.

phrases.translation: O believers! Eat from the good things We have provided for you.
phrases.explanation: Believers are asked to enjoy the wholesome provisions God has given them. The instruction recognizes food as a gift and guides people toward what is good. It connects everyday consumption with faith, inviting moderation and appreciation rather than treating material needs as separate from worship.

phrases.translation: And give thanks to Allah if you ˹truly˺ worship Him ˹alone˺
phrases.explanation: Gratitude to God is presented as a natural expression of sincere worship. Believers acknowledge the source of their provision and respond with thanks and obedience. The phrase links exclusive devotion with recognizing God’s gifts, showing that worship includes the way people appreciate and use what they receive.

phrases.translation: He has only forbidden you ˹to eat˺ carrion, blood, swine, and what is slaughtered in the name of any other than Allah.
phrases.explanation: The verse names foods prohibited for consumption: carrion, blood, pork, and what is dedicated in slaughter to another than God. These limits distinguish lawful eating from practices that violate divine guidance. The list is specific and does not imply that all food is forbidden, the passage also makes room for necessity.

phrases.translation: But if someone is compelled by necessity—
phrases.explanation: An exception is made for a person forced by genuine necessity. The law recognizes human vulnerability and does not demand that someone suffer or die when no permissible food is available. This qualification shows that divine instruction accounts for urgent circumstances rather than imposing hardship without compassion.

phrases.translation: neither driven by desire nor exceeding immediate need—they will not be sinful.
phrases.explanation: The exception applies when a person is not seeking prohibited food out of preference and does not exceed what necessity requires. The conditions preserve the prohibition while allowing survival. The verse balances clear boundaries with practical mercy for someone facing an unavoidable emergency.  This exception is narrow, preserving the rule while preventing avoidable harm.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: The verse closes by emphasizing God’s forgiveness and mercy. The exception reflects these attributes, assuring people that a necessary, limited response is not sinful. Divine law is presented with compassion and awareness of human need.  These attributes reassure the person that divine law recognizes necessity.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who hide Allah’s revelations, trading them for a fleeting gain consume nothing but fire into their bellies.
phrases.explanation: Those who conceal revelation for temporary worldly gain are warned with a vivid image of consuming fire. The metaphor conveys the spiritual danger of profiting from suppressed truth. The verse condemns deliberate deception and prioritizing short-lived advantage over the responsibility to communicate God’s guidance.  Their choice harms both their own integrity and those deprived of guidance.

phrases.translation: Allah will neither speak to them on the Day of Judgment,
phrases.explanation: The phrase describes a severe deprivation at judgment: they will not receive God’s favorable address. It emphasizes the seriousness of knowingly hiding revelation. The warning is not about ordinary silence but about rejection and condemnation in the final accounting.  The warning concerns the final encounter with God and the loss of favor.

phrases.translation: nor will He purify them.
phrases.explanation: They will not be cleansed from the consequences of their wrongdoing. The phrase underscores that deliberate concealment has lasting moral consequences unless one repents. It contrasts with the preceding promise that those who repent, reform, and disclose truth can receive forgiveness.  Purification would mean moral cleansing, which concealment has placed at risk.

phrases.translation: And they will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: The verse concludes with punishment for those who knowingly traded revelation for gain. The warning makes clear that worldly profit cannot compensate for the harm and accountability involved. It calls people entrusted with knowledge to communicate truth honestly.  The painful outcome is linked to deliberate deceit, not innocent ignorance.

phrases.translation: They are the ones who trade guidance for misguidance and forgiveness for punishment.
phrases.explanation: The verse portrays deliberate concealment as a disastrous exchange: people abandon guidance and the possibility of forgiveness for error and punishment. The imagery highlights how poor the bargain is, since fleeting benefit cannot match the lasting value of truth. It warns against choices that reverse moral priorities.

phrases.translation: How persistent are they in pursuit of the Fire
phrases.explanation: The rhetorical question expresses astonishment at their conduct, not admiration. Their choices lead toward punishment even as they pursue temporary advantage. The phrase emphasizes personal responsibility and calls readers to recognize the destination of harmful actions before it is too late.  The question emphasizes the absurdity of choosing punishment over guidance.

phrases.translation: That is because Allah has revealed the Book in truth.
phrases.explanation: The Book has been revealed with truth, providing a clear basis for guidance and judgment. The verse explains why rejecting or disputing it is serious. Revelation is not a human invention to be manipulated for gain, but a truthful message from God.  Truth provides a stable standard beyond changing interests or social pressure.

phrases.translation: And surely those who differ regarding it are totally engrossed in opposition
phrases.explanation: Those who dispute the Book in bad faith are described as deeply entrenched in opposition. The phrase criticizes obstinate contention, not sincere questions asked in search of understanding. It calls people to approach revelation honestly rather than turn disagreement into a means of resistance.  Honest inquiry differs from opposition that refuses to consider evidence.

phrases.translation: Righteousness is not in turning your faces towards the east or the west.
phrases.explanation: The verse clarifies that righteousness cannot be reduced to facing a particular direction in prayer. Ritual orientation matters when God commands it, but outward form alone does not define a virtuous life. The statement introduces a broader account joining belief, generosity, worship, integrity, and patience.

phrases.translation: Rather, the righteous are those who believe in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Books, and the prophets;
phrases.explanation: True righteousness begins with belief in God, the final judgment, angels, revealed Books, and the prophets. This faith gives moral life its foundation and connects believers to a shared history of revelation. The list shows that inward conviction is essential, while the rest of the verse details its outward expression.

phrases.translation: who give charity out of their cherished wealth to relatives, orphans, the poor, ˹needy˺ travellers, beggars, and for freeing captives;
phrases.explanation: Righteous people give from wealth they value to a range of people in need, including family, orphans, the poor, travelers, and captives. Generosity is meaningful because it involves real sacrifice and responds to concrete vulnerability. The list makes social responsibility central to the practice of faith.

phrases.translation: who establish prayer, pay alms-tax, and keep the pledges they make;
phrases.explanation: Righteousness includes regular prayer, the required alms-tax, and keeping promises. These practices join devotion to God with responsibility toward other people. The verse shows that faith is not only belief or private feeling, but a pattern of worship and trustworthy conduct.  These duties establish a consistent relationship with God and society.

phrases.translation: and who are patient in times of suffering, adversity, and in ˹the heat of˺ battle.
phrases.explanation: The righteous remain steadfast through personal suffering, hardship, and danger in battle. Patience here means perseverance in faith and moral duty, not indifference to pain. Including these trials shows that righteousness is tested in difficult circumstances, when commitment requires courage and endurance.  Their endurance includes remaining faithful when circumstances are especially severe.

phrases.translation: It is they who are true ˹in faith˺,
phrases.explanation: Those who combine belief with generosity, worship, integrity, and patience are described as truthful in faith. Their actions confirm the sincerity of their convictions. The verse rejects a merely verbal claim and presents consistent character as evidence of genuine belief.  This confirms that outward practice and inner belief belong together.

phrases.translation: and it is they who are mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.explanation: These people are mindful of God, keeping His guidance in view across worship and daily dealings. God-consciousness unites the qualities listed throughout the verse. The conclusion presents righteousness as an integrated life shaped by awareness of God and accountability to Him.  Their awareness shapes both private devotion and public responsibility.

phrases.translation: O believers! ˹The law of˺ retaliation is set for you in cases of murder—a free man for a free man, a slave for a slave, and a female for a female.
phrases.explanation: The verse establishes a legal framework for cases of murder, limiting retaliation rather than allowing uncontrolled revenge. Its historical wording addresses the parties and social categories of the context, while the principle is regulated justice. The following clauses also provide for pardon and compensation, showing that retaliation is not the only possible outcome.

phrases.translation: But if the offender is pardoned by the victim’s guardian,
phrases.explanation: The victim’s guardian may choose to pardon the offender, opening a path away from retaliation. This acknowledges the family’s role while making forgiveness possible. The verse does not force pardon, but presents it as a recognized option within a structured legal process.  Pardon can prevent the conflict from expanding into further loss of life.

phrases.translation: then blood-money should be decided fairly
phrases.explanation: If pardon is granted in exchange for compensation, the amount and terms should be fair. Justice requires that the agreement not become an excuse for exploitation or excess. The phrase makes fairness central to resolving the case through compensation.  Fair terms protect both sides and uphold the dignity of those involved.

phrases.translation: and payment should be made courteously.
phrases.explanation: The offender or responsible party is instructed to make payment in a proper and gracious manner. Courtesy prevents a settlement from being poisoned by humiliation or delay. The verse regulates both the agreement and the way people carry it out.  Good faith in payment helps restore trust after a devastating crime.

phrases.translation: This is a concession and a mercy from your Lord.
phrases.explanation: The allowance for pardon and compensation is described as divine mercy. It offers an alternative to retaliation while preserving justice and protecting life. The phrase encourages appreciation of a legal system that permits restraint and reconciliation.  Mercy is shown through the possibility of restraint and reconciliation.

phrases.translation: But whoever transgresses after that will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: Anyone who exceeds the limits after the settlement or ruling faces punishment. The warning guards against renewed vengeance and abuse of the concession. Justice requires respecting the agreed outcome rather than using a grave crime to justify further wrongdoing.  The law’s limits matter even after an emotionally painful offense.

phrases.translation: There is ˹security of˺ life for you in ˹the law of˺ retaliation,
phrases.explanation: Regulated retaliation protects life by deterring murder and preventing cycles of uncontrolled revenge. The verse presents law as a means of preserving life, not encouraging violence. By setting limits and recognizing pardon, the framework seeks justice while discouraging further bloodshed.  Clear limits can protect communities from repeated cycles of violence.

phrases.translation: O people of reason,
phrases.explanation: The appeal is directed to people capable of reflecting on consequences and justice. They are asked to look beyond an immediate desire for vengeance and consider how a fair legal framework protects society. Reasoned judgment is essential to understanding the purpose of the law.  The address invites thoughtful consideration of the law’s social purpose.

phrases.translation: so that you may become mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.explanation: The purpose includes growing in awareness of God and respecting the limits He has set. Mindfulness helps people avoid transgression even when grief and anger are powerful. The verse connects public justice with moral and spiritual responsibility.  Reverence for God encourages restraint and respect for human life.

phrases.translation: It is prescribed that when death approaches any of you—if they leave something of value—a will should be made in favour of parents and immediate family with fairness.
phrases.explanation: The verse instructs a person nearing death who has left wealth to make a fair bequest for parents and close relatives. The emphasis is on justice and care for family at a vulnerable moment. The rule belongs to the chapter’s broader concern for rights and responsible use of wealth, and is read alongside later inheritance guidance.

phrases.translation: ˹This is˺ an obligation on those who are mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.explanation: The bequest is presented as an obligation for people conscious of God. Mindfulness should shape how wealth is distributed and prevent neglect of family responsibilities. The phrase frames the instruction as a matter of accountability, not merely personal preference.  Fair provision can reduce conflict and protect vulnerable family members.

phrases.translation: But whoever changes the will after hearing it, the blame will only be on those who made the change.
phrases.explanation: A will should not be altered after it has been heard and understood, except through a just resolution such as the one described in the next verse. Responsibility for an unjust change rests on those who make it, not the person who originally gave the instruction. This protects the integrity of a final bequest.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: God hears the instructions and knows the intentions behind any alteration. People may conceal manipulation from relatives, but not from God. These attributes affirm accountability and encourage honesty in handling a will.  The reminder discourages treating private dealings as beyond moral scrutiny.  Divine knowledge makes ethical conduct necessary even when no human witness is present.

phrases.translation: Whoever suspects an error or an injustice in the will and brings about a ˹fair˺ settlement among the parties will not be sinful.
phrases.explanation: A person who notices an error or unfairness may mediate a just settlement. Correcting injustice is not the same as selfishly changing a will, and the verse removes blame from fair reconciliation. It encourages responsible intervention when beneficiaries might otherwise be harmed.  Mediators should act impartially and preserve the rights of all beneficiaries.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: God’s forgiveness and mercy frame the process of correction and settlement. The attributes reassure those who seek fairness and remind all parties to act with compassion. The verse presents justice within family affairs as consistent with divine mercy.  The divine attributes encourage people to settle disputes without vindictiveness.

phrases.translation: O believers!
phrases.explanation: The address identifies the community responsible for the fasting command. It signals a shared act of worship that will shape individual habits and collective life. The instruction is directed to believers as a practice of faith, not merely a dietary rule.  The practice is a communal marker of obedience and spiritual discipline.

phrases.translation: Fasting is prescribed for you—as it was for those before you—
phrases.explanation: Fasting is established as an obligation for this community and is connected to religious communities before it. The shared practice places Muslim fasting within a wider history of devotion. Its purpose is spiritual formation, not hardship for its own sake.  Its historical continuity shows fasting is a recognized form of worship.

phrases.translation: so perhaps you will become mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.explanation: The intended outcome is greater God-consciousness. By restraining permissible desires for a set time, believers practice self-control and awareness of God. Fasting trains people to choose obedience and compassion, making mindfulness the central aim of the obligation.  Self-restraint can strengthen empathy and help believers resist harmful impulses.

phrases.translation: ˹Fast a˺ prescribed number of days.
phrases.explanation: Fasting is required for a defined period, not indefinitely. This gives the obligation a clear and manageable scope. The phrase introduces accommodations for people whose circumstances make fasting difficult and shows that the practice is structured.  The limited duration helps people understand the obligation and plan for it.

phrases.translation: But whoever of you is ill or on a journey, then ˹let them fast˺ an equal number of days ˹after Ramaḍân˺.
phrases.explanation: People who are ill or traveling may make up missed fasts later for an equal number of days. The allowance recognizes real hardship while preserving the obligation. It balances devotion with practical care and prevents temporary circumstances from becoming a permanent loss of worship.  The missed days are made up when the temporary difficulty has passed.

phrases.translation: For those who can only fast with extreme difficulty, compensation can be made by feeding a needy person ˹for every day not fasted˺.
phrases.explanation: The verse provides compensation through feeding someone in need for those unable to fast except with extreme difficulty. This connects worship with care for the vulnerable. It recognizes limits in human capacity and gives a concrete way to fulfill responsibility where fasting is exceptionally burdensome.

phrases.translation: But whoever volunteers to give more, it is better for them.
phrases.explanation: Those who voluntarily give beyond the required compensation do good. The phrase encourages generosity without making extra giving compulsory. It shows how the fasting rules can inspire concern for others and make worship a source of social benefit.  Voluntary generosity adds benefit for the recipient and reward for the giver.

phrases.translation: And to fast is better for you, if only you knew
phrases.explanation: Fasting remains better for those able to observe it, despite the accommodations for hardship. The verse affirms its spiritual value while maintaining compassion for those who need allowances. Its benefit may be deeper than people immediately perceive, including discipline and mindfulness.  The verse encourages fasting while preserving compassion for exceptional hardship.

phrases.translation: Ramaḍân is the month in which the Quran was revealed as a guide for humanity with clear proofs of guidance and the standard ˹to distinguish between right and wrong˺.
phrases.explanation: Ramaḍân is honored as the month when the Qur’an began to be revealed. The scripture guides humanity, provides clear evidence, and distinguishes truth from falsehood. The verse links fasting with gratitude for revelation, making the month a time of worship and renewed engagement with divine guidance.

phrases.translation: So whoever is present this month, let them fast.
phrases.explanation: Those who are present and able during Ramaḍân are commanded to fast. The rule anchors the obligation to the month associated with the Qur’an’s revelation. The following clause again provides an allowance for illness and travel, demonstrating that the command is balanced with care.  The instruction applies to those who meet the conditions for fasting.

phrases.translation: But whoever is ill or on a journey, then ˹let them fast˺ an equal number of days ˹after Ramaḍân˺.
phrases.explanation: The allowance for illness and travel is repeated to ensure that people understand how to handle missed days. They make up an equal number afterward. This repetition highlights that divine instruction recognizes circumstances and does not require people to endanger health or endure undue difficulty.

phrases.translation: Allah intends ease for you, not hardship,
phrases.explanation: The rule is explicitly framed as intended ease. God’s law does not seek unnecessary hardship, and the allowances demonstrate compassion. This principle helps believers understand the fasting instructions as a coherent practice that accommodates genuine human needs.  The principle of ease governs how the entire obligation should be understood.

phrases.translation: so that you may complete the prescribed period and proclaim the greatness of Allah for guiding you,
phrases.explanation: Believers complete the fasting days and glorify God for the guidance He has given. Completion and praise are joined: fasting is both an act of obedience and a response to revelation. The phrase directs attention from the physical discipline toward gratitude for spiritual direction.  Completing the days expresses commitment to the full prescribed act of worship.

phrases.translation: and perhaps you will be grateful
phrases.explanation: Gratitude is the hoped-for result of fasting and guidance. Believers recognize the Qur’an, the ability to worship, and divine accommodations as blessings. The verse concludes by connecting discipline with thankfulness rather than self-congratulation.  Gratitude recognizes both revelation and the opportunity to respond to it.  The monthly practice thus becomes a recurring occasion for renewed appreciation.

phrases.translation: When My servants ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about Me:
phrases.explanation: The verse addresses questions about God with a direct divine response. Rather than placing distance between God and the person praying, it emphasizes immediate nearness. The personal wording offers reassurance to anyone seeking connection and guidance through prayer.  The answer is immediate, making clear that prayer is open to every servant.

phrases.translation: I am truly near.
phrases.explanation: God declares His nearness to His servants. This is nearness in knowledge, care, and response, not a claim that God is physically contained in a place. The statement reassures believers that prayer is heard and that they can turn to God directly.  This reassurance invites sincere reliance rather than despair or distance.

phrases.translation: I respond to one’s prayer when they call upon Me.
phrases.explanation: God responds to those who call upon Him. Response may take forms and timing known to God, so the phrase encourages sincere prayer rather than demanding a particular outcome. It affirms that no call is ignored and that people may approach God without intermediaries.  The promise encourages persistence even when an answer is not immediately visible.

phrases.translation: So let them respond ˹with obedience˺ to Me and believe in Me,
phrases.explanation: Prayer is paired with obedience and faith. Believers are called to respond to God’s guidance just as they ask Him for help. This reciprocity presents prayer as part of a relationship grounded in trust, commitment, and action.  Faith and obedience show that the relationship is reciprocal and committed.

phrases.translation: perhaps they will be guided ˹to the Right Way˺
phrases.explanation: Faithful response to God’s call leads toward guidance. Prayer is not isolated from conduct, but supports a life oriented by divine instruction. The verse ends with hope that those who call on God and obey Him will find the right path.  Guidance is a lasting benefit beyond receiving a particular requested favor.

phrases.translation: It has been made permissible for you to be intimate with your wives during the nights preceding the fast.
phrases.explanation: Intimacy between spouses is permitted during the nights of fasting. The instruction clarifies the boundaries of the fast and removes uncertainty about marital life after sunset. It treats lawful intimacy as part of ordinary human life within limits set by God.  This clarification removes doubt and protects the fasting practice from confusion.

phrases.translation: Your spouses are a garment for you as you are for them.
phrases.explanation: The image of spouses as garments for one another conveys closeness, mutual care, and protection. The relationship is reciprocal rather than one-sided. The phrase honors intimacy within marriage and emphasizes the comfort and dignity spouses should provide each other.  The metaphor conveys mutual intimacy, care, and the sharing of private life.

phrases.translation: Allah knows that you were deceiving yourselves.
phrases.explanation: God knew that some believers had struggled to observe the earlier restriction and had acted against it. The phrase acknowledges human weakness honestly rather than concealing it. Divine knowledge makes the subsequent pardon and clarification an act of mercy and practical guidance.  God’s knowledge provides the basis for a rule that addresses actual human experience.

phrases.translation: So He has accepted your repentance and pardoned you.
phrases.explanation: God accepts repentance and forgives the believers who turned back after their missteps. The verse offers reassurance that failure need not become permanent when people repent sincerely. It presents the clarification of the rule alongside forgiveness and compassion.  The pardon shows that sincere repentance can follow a mistaken action.

phrases.translation: So now you may be intimate with them and seek what Allah has prescribed for you.
phrases.explanation: Spouses are now permitted intimacy during the nights, and believers may seek what God has made lawful and beneficial. The instruction encourages them to follow the clarified rule without shame. It directs desire within divinely established boundaries.  The permission applies within the nights and does not remove the daytime fast.

phrases.translation: ˹You may˺ eat and drink until you see the light of dawn breaking the darkness of night,
phrases.explanation: Eating and drinking remain permitted through the night until dawn becomes distinguishable. The phrase defines when the daily fast begins. Its clear timing helps believers practice the obligation consistently while allowing nourishment during the permitted hours.  The visible dawn offers a practical sign for beginning daily abstention.

phrases.translation: then complete the fast until nightfall.
phrases.explanation: The fast continues from dawn until nightfall. This marks the daily period of abstention and gives the practice a clear beginning and end. The instruction is practical, making the rhythm of fasting understandable and shared by the community.  The time limit makes the daily worship clear and consistent for all.

phrases.translation: Do not be intimate with your spouses while you are meditating in the mosques.
phrases.explanation: During devotional retreat in a mosque, marital intimacy is not permitted. The restriction protects the focused nature of the retreat. The verse distinguishes this period from ordinary nights of fasting and clarifies that worship has particular boundaries.  Devotional retreat has conditions that distinguish it from ordinary married life.

phrases.translation: These are the limits set by Allah, so do not exceed them.
phrases.explanation: The fasting and retreat rules are described as limits established by God. Believers are asked to respect those boundaries rather than treat them casually. The phrase emphasizes that knowing the detailed permissions and restrictions is part of mindful obedience.  Clear limits protect the integrity of worship and prevent self-serving exceptions.

phrases.translation: This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to people, so they may become mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.explanation: God clarifies these rules so people can understand and observe them with mindfulness. Clear guidance supports worship without unnecessary confusion. The verse concludes by connecting practical instruction to the broader goal of God-conscious living.  Understanding the rules helps people practice them with sincere awareness.  Mindfulness guides believers to respect both the permission and the restriction.

phrases.translation: Do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly,
phrases.explanation: People are forbidden to take or use one another’s wealth through unjust means. The principle protects property and discourages exploitation, fraud, and coercion. It applies broadly to economic dealings and makes justice essential to how wealth is acquired.  Fair exchange depends on consent, honesty, and respect for other people’s rights.

phrases.translation: nor deliberately bribe authorities in order to devour a portion of others’ property,
phrases.explanation: The verse specifically condemns using bribery or legal manipulation to seize another person’s property. Appearing to have official approval does not make an unjust claim lawful. The warning protects people from corruption that disguises theft as legitimate procedure.  The use of influence cannot turn an unjust transfer into a rightful one.

phrases.translation: knowing that it is a sin
phrases.explanation: The wrongdoing is especially serious when people know their conduct is sinful. Awareness removes the excuse of ignorance and emphasizes deliberate responsibility. The verse calls for integrity in disputes and warns against exploiting institutions to enrich oneself unjustly.  The warning urges people to resist greed even when wrongdoing seems advantageous.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about the phases of the moon.
phrases.explanation: People ask about the changing appearances of the moon. The answer addresses the practical purpose of these phases rather than offering abstract speculation. The question introduces a teaching about how natural cycles support communal timing and religious observance.  Their regular pattern makes the moon a practical marker for the calendar.

phrases.translation: Say, “They are a means for people to determine time and pilgrimage.”
phrases.explanation: The lunar phases help people measure time and know when to perform pilgrimage. The moon’s visible changes provide a shared calendar for ordinary life and worship. The answer highlights the practical wisdom of creation and links observation of nature with religious practice.  This shared timing helps communities coordinate both worship and daily affairs.

phrases.translation: Righteousness is not in entering your houses from the back doors.
phrases.explanation: The verse rejects a customary practice of entering homes through their backs as a supposed act of righteousness. Outward rituals without divine basis do not create true piety. The statement redirects attention from inherited superstition to the real meaning of God-consciousness.  The verse critiques a particular custom, not ordinary respect for tradition.

phrases.translation: Rather, righteousness is to be mindful ˹of Allah˺.
phrases.explanation: True righteousness is grounded in mindfulness of God. This inner orientation shapes ethical behavior and obedience more deeply than arbitrary customs. The phrase provides a concise principle for distinguishing genuine devotion from practices that merely appear religious.  Awareness of God should shape conduct rather than rely on superstition.

phrases.translation: So enter your homes through their ˹proper˺ doors,
phrases.explanation: People are told to enter homes through their proper doors, following ordinary and sensible practice. The instruction replaces an unfounded custom with clear guidance. It illustrates that religion does not require needless difficulty or ritualized behavior without sound reason.  Ordinary actions can be performed simply without inventing ritual obstacles.

phrases.translation: and be mindful of Allah so you may be successful
phrases.explanation: The verse returns to God-consciousness as the path to success. Mindfulness helps people follow genuine guidance and avoid empty customs. The conclusion links spiritual awareness with a flourishing life grounded in obedience and sound judgment.  Success comes through obedience rooted in sincere awareness of God.

phrases.translation: Fight in the cause of Allah ˹only˺ against those who wage war against you,
phrases.explanation: The verse permits fighting in God’s cause against those who wage war, framing it as defensive and constrained. It does not authorize indiscriminate violence or attack on people who are not fighting. The qualification establishes the context and limits of armed conflict.  The restriction protects noncombatants and prevents aggression against others.

phrases.translation: but do not exceed the limits.
phrases.explanation: Even in conflict, believers must not transgress. The command rules out excess and requires restraint under God’s moral boundaries. Fighting does not suspend justice or permit harm beyond what is allowed, making ethical limits integral to the instruction.  The command remains binding even when conflict and anger are intense.

phrases.translation: Allah does not like transgressors
phrases.explanation: God’s disapproval of transgression reinforces the restriction. Believers cannot justify excess by invoking the cause of God. The phrase makes clear that divine support is not for wrongdoing and calls for disciplined conduct even amid conflict.  The warning prevents people from using religious language to excuse abuse.

phrases.translation: Kill them wherever you come upon them and drive them out of the places from which they have driven you out.
phrases.explanation: This command occurs within a passage addressing armed persecution and expulsion, not as permission for indiscriminate violence. It refers to confronting those who had driven the believers from their homes. The surrounding limits, including the sacred sanctuary and the command to stop when aggression ends, govern how this instruction is understood.

phrases.translation: For persecution is far worse than killing.
phrases.explanation: The verse condemns persecution as a grave wrong, describing it as worse than killing in this conflict context. Oppression that prevents people from practicing their faith and drives them from home is not treated as harmless. The statement explains the defensive struggle while not excusing excess or aggression.

phrases.translation: And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque unless they attack you there.
phrases.explanation: Fighting is prohibited at the Sacred Mosque unless the other side attacks there first. This special restriction protects the sanctuary and limits the conflict even under severe pressure. The verse makes clear that the believers are not to initiate violence in this sacred place.  The exception remains narrowly tied to immediate self-defense.

phrases.translation: If they do so, then fight them—that is the reward of the disbelievers
phrases.explanation: If the opponents initiate an attack at the sanctuary, the believers may defend themselves. The consequence is tied to the aggressors’ action, not a general license to attack all disbelievers. This clause maintains the defensive context and warns that those who choose aggression bear its consequences.

phrases.translation: But if they cease, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: If the opponents stop their persecution and aggression, fighting must cease. God’s forgiveness and mercy provide the reason not to continue hostility after its cause has ended. The verse prioritizes restraint and the possibility of reconciliation, rather than treating conflict as an end in itself.

phrases.translation: Fight against them ˹if they persecute you˺ until there is no more persecution,
phrases.explanation: The stated aim is to end persecution, not to wage unlimited war. The bracketed context makes clear that fighting concerns those who oppress and attack the believers. The goal is that people are no longer coerced or driven from worship, after which the command to stop applies.

phrases.translation: and ˹your˺ devotion will be to Allah ˹alone˺.
phrases.explanation: The purpose is freedom to devote worship to God alone, without coercion or persecution. It is not a call to force belief, but to end the oppression that obstructs religious practice. The phrase connects the struggle to protection of sincere worship.  Protection of religious freedom is the stated end of the fighting.

phrases.translation: If they stop ˹persecuting you˺, let there be no hostility except against the aggressors
phrases.explanation: When persecution ends, hostility must also end, apart from dealing with those who continue aggression. This limit rules out revenge against people who have ceased fighting. The verse repeatedly binds conflict to the presence of aggression and directs believers toward restraint.  The qualification leaves no basis for continued fighting after peace.
